result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.common_neighbors()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the number of common neighbors for node pairs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L8732-L8810){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.common_neighbors(ebunch=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For each pair of nodes `(u, v)`, counts how many nodes are neighbors of both `u` and `v`. Common neighbors is a simple but effective link prediction measure. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ebunch]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[Union[int, str], Union[int, str]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : List of node pairs to compute predictions for. Each pair can use node IDs (integers) or labels (strings). If `None`, computes for all pairs of nodes that are not already connected. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of `(u, v, count)` tuples where count is the number of common neighbors. Results are returned with node IDs. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: O(k^2) per pair where k is the average degree - works best for social networks with high clustering - simple baseline for link prediction tasks - higher count suggests higher likelihood of future connection ## Examples {.doc-examples} Predict missing links in a social network: ::: {#24c6b5a9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) for name in ["Alice", "Bob", "Carol", "Dave"]: graph.add_node(label=name) # Alice and Carol share Bob as a friend graph.add_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob") graph.add_edge(source="Carol", target="Bob") graph.add_edge(source="Carol", target="Dave") # Check common neighbors for unconnected pairs predictions = graph.common_neighbors() for u, v, count in predictions: # Prints e.g., "1 - 3: 1 common neighbors" f"{u} - {v}: {count} common neighbors" ``` ::: Check specific pairs: ::: {#d3eb452c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) for name in ["Alice", "Bob", "Carol", "Dave"]: graph.add_node(label=name) graph.add_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob") graph.add_edge(source="Carol", target="Bob") pairs = [("Alice", "Carol"), ("Alice", "Dave")] predictions = graph.common_neighbors(pairs) # Alice-Carol have 1 common neighbor (Bob) # Alice-Dave have 0 common neighbors ``` :::
